title: Κάνθαροι δύο
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 149 (= Perry 84). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔν τινι νησιδίῳ ταῦρος ἐνέμετο· τῇ δὲ τούτου κόπρῳ κάνθαροι ἐτρέφοντο δύο.
sentences.tr: En tini nēsidiōi tauros enemeto· tēi de toutou koprōi kantharoi etrephonto dyo.
sentences.l: On a certain little island a bull was grazing; and on his dung two beetles were feeding.
sentences.n: νησίδιον is the diminutive of νῆσος, a scrap of an island — and its smallness is the whole premise. ἐνέμετο and ἐτρέφοντο are both middle, what an animal does for itself; the dative τῇ κόπρῳ is the means. Chambry's ano teleia (·) marks a stop lighter than a full stop.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ τοῦ χειμῶνος ἐνισταμένου, ὁ ἕτερος ἔλεγε πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον ὡς ἄρα βούλοιτο εἰς τὴν ἤπειρον διαπτάσθαι, ἵνα ἐκείνῳ μόνῳ ὄντι ἡ τροφὴ ἱκανῶς ὑπάρχῃ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκεῖσε ἐλθὼν τὸν χειμῶνα διαγένηται.
sentences.tr: Kai dē tou cheimōnos enistamenou, ho heteros elege pros ton heteron hōs ara bouloito eis tēn ēpeiron diaptasthai, hina ekeinōi monōi onti hē trophē hikanōs hyparchēi, kai autos ekeise elthōn ton cheimōna diagenētai.
sentences.l: And indeed, winter setting in, the one said to the other that he wished, so he claimed, to fly across to the mainland, so that for that one, being alone, the food might be sufficient, and he himself, having gone thither, might get through the winter.
sentences.i: And when winter was setting in, the one told the other that he had a mind to fly across to the mainland, so that his companion, left alone, might have food enough, while he himself would go over there and see the winter out.
sentences.n: τοῦ χειμῶνος ἐνισταμένου is a genitive absolute. ὡς … βούλοιτο is indirect speech after a verb of saying, the optative standing in for the indicative of his own words; ἄρα colours the report with the reporter's reserve, "so he gave out". The purpose clause with ἵνα keeps the subjunctive. The generosity is stated first and the beetle's own advantage second.

sentences.t: Ἔλεγε δὲ ὅτι, ἐὰν πολλὴν εὕρῃ τὴν νομήν, καὶ αὐτῷ οἴσει.
sentences.tr: Elege de hoti, ean pollēn heurēi tēn nomēn, kai autōi oisei.
sentences.l: And he said that, if he finds the pasture plentiful, he will bring some for him too.
sentences.i: And he said that if he found the feeding plentiful, he would bring some back for his friend as well.
sentences.n: ὅτι here introduces indirect speech that keeps the words as spoken — ἐάν with the subjunctive and the future οἴσει are what he actually said. οἴσει is the future of φέρω, supplied from a different root. What is to be brought is never named.

sentences.t: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς τὴν χέρσον καὶ καταλαβὼν πολλὴν μὲν τὴν κόπρον, ὑγρὰν δέ, μένων ἐτρέφετο ἐνταῦθα.
sentences.tr: Paragenomenos de eis tēn cherson kai katalabōn pollēn men tēn kopron, hygran de, menōn etrepheto entautha.
sentences.l: And having arrived at the dry land and having found the dung plentiful indeed, but wet, remaining he fed there.
sentences.i: And when he had reached the mainland and found the dung plentiful, but wet, he stayed and fed there.
sentences.n: μέν and δέ balance two adjectives on the one noun: plentiful, yes — but wet. The wetness is not scene-painting; a beetle carries dung by rolling it into a ball, and wet dung will not roll.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ χειμῶνος διελθόντος, πάλιν εἰς τὴν νῆσον διέπτη.
sentences.tr: Tou de cheimōnos dielthontos, palin eis tēn nēson dieptē.
sentences.l: And winter having gone by, he flew across again to the island.
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute, matching the one that opened the journey; the two frame the absence. διέπτη is the aorist of διαπέτομαι, the same verb as the infinitive διαπτάσθαι above.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ἕτερος θεασάμενος αὐτὸν λιπαρὸν καὶ εὐεκτοῦντα, ᾐτιάσατο αὐτὸν διότι προϋποσχόμενος αὐτῷ οὐδὲν ἐκόμισεν.
sentences.tr: Ho de heteros theasamenos auton liparon kai euektounta, ēitiasato auton dioti proyposchomenos autōi ouden ekomisen.
sentences.l: And the other, having beheld him sleek and in good condition, laid it to his charge that, having promised him beforehand, he had brought nothing.
sentences.i: And the other, seeing him sleek and thriving, reproached him for bringing nothing after promising he would.
sentences.n: αἰτιάομαι takes the accusative of the person charged; διότι, "for the reason that", gives the charge itself. προϋποσχόμενος is the aorist middle participle of προϋπισχνέομαι, "promise in advance", and the diaeresis on ϋ shows that the ου of προ-υπ- is not a diphthong. λιπαρός is the glisten of a well-fed body, which is evidence against him before he speaks.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἶπε· « Μὴ ἐμὲ μέμφου, τὴν δὲ φύσιν τοῦ τόπου· ἐκεῖθεν γὰρ τρέφεσθαι μὲν οἷόν τε, φέρεσθαι δὲ οὐδέν. »
sentences.tr: Ho de eipe· « Mē eme memphou, tēn de physin tou topou· ekeithen gar trephesthai men hoion te, pheresthai de ouden. »
sentences.l: And he said: « Blame not me, but the nature of the place; for from there one may feed oneself, but carry nothing away. »
sentences.n: μὴ μέμφου is a present imperative with μή, the negative that belongs to commands. οἷόν τε (ἐστί) is the standing idiom for "it is possible", and the two infinitives under it are held apart by μέν and δέ. The excuse is true as far as it goes: he never says he tried.

sentences.t: Οὗτος ὁ λόγος ἁρμόσειεν ἂν πρὸς ἐκείνους οἳ τὰς φιλίας μέχρις ἑστιάσεως μόνον παρέχονται, περαιτέρω δὲ οὐδὲν τοὺς φίλους ὠφελοῦσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtos ho logos harmoseien an pros ekeinous hoi tas philias mechris hestiaseōs monon parechontai, peraiterō de ouden tous philous ōphelousin.
sentences.l: This story would fit those who furnish their friendships only as far as a feast, and beyond that benefit their friends in nothing.
sentences.i: This story would fit those who offer their friendship only as far as the dinner table, and beyond that do their friends no good at all.
sentences.n: ἁρμόσειεν ἄν is a potential optative, "would fit" — a shade more guarded than the ἁρμόττει this closing formula usually carries. μέχρις with the genitive marks the limit reached, ἑστίασις being the entertaining of a guest at table. ὠφελέω takes the accusative of the person helped.
